description: The bar chart titled “Average performance on November 2024 AMC 10/12 tests” compares the average scores (at temperature = 0.5) of various large language models on standardized math tests, with scores ranging from approximately 66 to 92. The horizontal axis lists nine models: Llama-3.3 70B Instruct, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Qwen 2.5 14B-Instruct, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen 2.5 72B-Instruct, Gemini Flash 1.5, Gemini Pro 1.5, and phi-4. The vertical axis represents the average score, scaled from 60 to 90 in increments of 10. Each model has two bars: a light blue bar labeled “Small model” and a dark blue bar labeled “Small model” in the legend — though this appears to be a labeling error, as the legend shows two identical entries; visually, the light blue bars correspond to the first model in each pair (e.g., Llama-3.3, Claude 3.5, etc.), and the dark blue bars correspond to the second (e.g., Qwen 2.5, GPT-4o, etc.). Notably, phi-4 (dark blue) achieves the highest score at 91.8, followed closely by Gemini Pro 1.5 (light blue) at 89.8. The lowest score is Llama-3.3 70B Instruct (light blue) at 66.4. Error bars are present on each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals, though their exact magnitude is not quantified. The chart visually emphasizes phi-4’s top performance, with its bar being the tallest and most rightward. The data suggests a general trend of newer or more specialized models (like phi-4 and Gemini Pro 1.5) outperforming earlier or more general-purpose models on this specific math benchmark.
